claims.text: Cold-sprayed hard, nanocrystalline nickel-based alloy can repair localized surface damage on a high-value component.
The cold-sprayed repair resists hot cracking better than a traditional fusion-welded repair.
The cold-sprayed repair has higher surface hardness than a fusion-welded repair and an untreated surface.
The cold-sprayed repair has greater wear resistance than a fusion-welded repair and an untreated surface.
The cold-sprayed repair has greater corrosion resistance than a fusion-welded repair and an untreated surface.
Cold spray can be applied at ambient to slightly elevated processing temperatures below 150°C in an inert-gas environment while avoiding thermal damage.
Cold spray produces a dense, mechanically bonded coating with a refined nanocrystalline microstructure and minimal defects.
The coating isolates the substrate from corrosive and abrasive exposure.
Cold spray accelerates alloy powder particles to high velocities.
High-velocity particle impact causes severe plastic deformation.
Impact deformation creates mechanical interlocking and a fine-grained, highly adherent deposit.
The deposit forms without reaching melting temperatures.
Avoiding melting reduces the thermal stresses and hot cracking associated with fusion welding.
Fusion-welding repair introduces a high thermal load and may produce undesirable microstructural changes.
Untreated surfaces undergo accelerated damage under aggressive service conditions.
The predicted improvements persist during corrosive exposure, cyclic mechanical loading, and moderate-temperature service up to approximately 200°C.
Performance may diminish outside the stated service range.

contradictions.description: The design prepares only cold-sprayed and fusion-welded specimen sets, but the falsification rule also requires comparison with untreated surfaces. No untreated control set is included in the stated design.
